messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: Elevated 5xx rate observed on VPC peering vpc-peer-1234 -> transit (euw3b). Automated detection flagged route asymmetry and packet loss. Affected prefixes: 10.20.0.0/16, 10.30.5.0/24. Pager to oncall.

iris (oncall): ack — picking up. Starting triage. Who's on net infra?
joel-net: i'm free, i'll join. seeing duplicate BGP path advertisements from partner at AS 64512, path prepends sometimes, AS path inconsistent -> likely route leak or community misfiltering.
ben-sre: also seeing 5xx spike in routing-proxy logs, connection resets to privateconnect endpoints in eu-west-3b.
iris (oncall): @joel-net please confirm BGP session states and recent route updates. @ria-cs can you DM affected customers list? need impact scope.
joel-net: running quick checks — grabbing BGP RIB.
joel-net: ```
net> show ip bgp neighbors 203.0.113.21 received-routes | tail -n 20
* 10.20.0.0/16    64512 64498 0. localpref 100
* 10.30.5.0/24    64512    0
``` 
joel-net: looks like partner suddenly started advertising /16 and /24 with inconsistent next-hops; some nodes prefer the /16 via partner rather than our peering -> traffic salted to wrong AZ.
netinfra-bot: route-table-propagation = delayed for vpc-6789 in euw3b, last sync 11s ago.
ben-sre: can we force route withdraw for the /16 to prefer our internal path (announce more-specific /20) as a mitigation?
iris (oncall): agree. @joel-net prep a temporary more-specific advertisement for 10.20.0.0/20 from our transit to steer traffic back. also lower DNS TTL for impacted services to 30s -- @ria-cs coordinate with customers.
joel-net: preparing BGP change now. will announce /20 from edge with higher localpref.
joel-net: ```
bgp> neighbor 203.0.113.21 route-map SET-LOCALPREF out
route-map SET-LOCALPREF permit 10
 set local-preference 200
```
ben-sre: applying ephemeral route-map on edge proxies as well to avoid immediate 5xx blowups. notify if error counts drop.
ben-sre: metric snapshot: 5xx rate peaked at 22/min previous 5m -> now 7/min and decreasing.
ria-cs: Customer notify: DM'd AcmeCorp, BetaApps, DataVault and 3 smaller tenants. AcmeCorp reported failed API calls and sessions dropping to private endpoints — they've applied a temporary retry/backoff.
iris (oncall): good. @netops please open support ticket to partner (AS64512) and request they stop advertising aggregated /16 until we finish cutover.
netops: open ticket: INC-7721 to peer ops. added logs and traceroute. ETA partner reply 28m.
joel-net: traceroute from euw3b->onprem shows first hop change when peer advertises /16, causing packet steering to wrong colo.
joel-net: ```
traceroute to 203.0.113.200 (203.0.113.200), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1) 0.4 ms 0.3 ms 0.3 ms
 2 198.51.100.2 (198.51.100.2) 1.2 ms 1.3 ms 1.1 ms
 3 * * *
``` 
ben-sre: after /20 announce, 5xx now below 1/min and error rate normalizing.
ria-cs: customers acknowledged improved connectivity, AcmeCorp reported 90% reduction in failed requests.
iris (oncall): keeping thread open for handoff. I'll stay 15m for validation then pass to day SRE. prepare short incident blurb for status page.
sre-runbook-bot: Suggested follow-ups: capture BGP updates, export route snapshots, and schedule postmortem with partner ops. runbook link: https://runbooks/internal/vpc-peering-leak.
iris (oncall): creating incident record IN-2248009876 with initial mitigation steps.
ben-sre: adding timeline and packet captures to the ticket.
ria-cs: posting customer-facing note draft to #customer-commms for review.
iris (oncall): handing to @ben-sre for next 2 hours. Ben, you're owner for postmortem and action items (filters, community tags, monitor thresholds).
ben-sre: taking handoff. will coordinate with netops to implement stricter prefix filters and add BGP community-based route suppression.
joel-net: followup action: add RPKI and more-specific prefix limits on transit, request partner to patch their aggregation config.
iris (oncall): thanks all. :thumbsup: closing pager. last check in 15m.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: immediate mitigation applied, 5xx rates restored. Incident will be reviewed during next oncall rotation.

-- thread notes: short-term mitigation was to announce /20 to override partner /16; root cause suspected partner-side aggregate advertisement causing route asymmetry and DNS TTL interactions. Postmortem needed to ensure permanent filters and SLA update for partner.
